_comment: 1.12.2 line against legacy Just Enough Items 4.16.x, running the standalone in-client UI test harness (uitest/1.12.2-forge, an independent ForgeGradle 7 legacy-mode Gradle build in this repository, shared by both 1.12.2 rows) through the three-stage pipeline config->build->test: jt resolves and pins, builds/reuses the JECh srg jar from the 1.12.0 checkout and compiles the harness build, then launches that build's runClient with the jars under test as -PjechJar/-PjeiJar — the row is picked by the JEI-line jar's own filename, the build stages no choice of its own. The client drives the scenarios itself and writes report.json, its captures and junit.xml before it quits itself; that is why the row declares no ready_when (stopping this client early would kill it mid-scenario and leave no report) and no world (the level asserted against is the one the harness's runner creates and pins itself). No gradle block: the harness build is the launch layer. jech and jei both carry via=dev-classpath, each for its own measured reason: the JECh srg jar rides the run task's classpath, where FML's ModDiscoverer.findClasspathMods discovers the jecharacters mod in it and the dev run's FMLDeobfuscationTransformer maps its SRG member references into the run's MCP names at load time; the JEI-line jar has to be staged by the build itself with its access transformer remapped, because a published 1.12.2 AT is written in SRG member names that never match the MCP-named members a dev client has — a raw staged copy dies in JEI's init with IllegalAccessError on TextureMap.initMissingImage (measured; the build's stageUiTestDevMod does the remap, fail-closed on a rule without an MCP name in its comment). java.version 21 is the JDK the harness build's Gradle wrapper itself runs on (Gradle 9.8.1 cannot start on the row's client JDK 8); the client stays on the build's own toolchain 8. The narrative and the earlier measurements are in envs/README.md, 'The 1.12.2 rows and the gradle launch'. No 'Registering JEI pinyin search index' check here: that line is emitted by JechJeiPlugin.registerAdvancedSearch, and legacy JEI 4.16.1.301 has no mezz/jei/api/IAdvancedSearchRegistry to implement (75 classes under mezz/jei/api, none of them the search API; HEI 4.34.0 has it). With legacy JEI the integration is the classic ASM path instead -- its two markers below are the assertion, and the extra check pins the suffix-tree patch only this path applies.
